item.text: I’m pulling the recorded project knowledge directly so I can enumerate the current Lesson entries exhaustively rather than guessing from code.

content.text:
Relevant recorded knowledge (23 items):

• Lesson — "Value-ref wiring check is load-bearing"
  hasDescription: Adding value-reference coverage for a language must start by checking the language's declarator node types and file/class/module scope behavior, because a wrong node type or scope assumption can make the feature silently emit nothing or emit wrong edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 says §5 steps A-C are where languages differ, where most real decisions are, and must not be skipped.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/8a2d2161-956f-4866-8898-ba1a5a9346a9
  hasTitle: Value-ref wiring check is load-bearing
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/a9dbeadd-633e-4f81-8ccf-af725f149cf5

• Lesson — "Measure before assuming holes"
  hasDescription: Measure framework usage before assuming a dynamic-dispatch hole; Svelte's presumed event-handler gap was not the real gap because modern Svelte often uses form actions and callback props instead of `on:click={fn}`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 explicitly states this lesson in the Svelte/SvelteKit row.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/d7d0f887-a173-47b9-9cd8-3f4d9dc5d9f6
  hasTitle: Measure before assuming holes
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-22T23:16:11Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/e06e3285-0e7b-4a1b-83ae-4e45a50f9e6f

• Constraint — "Phase one bridge gate"
  hasDescription: Phase 2 must not begin until Swift-Objective-C bridging passes the mixed iOS §5a validation bar on Charts, Realm-Cocoa, and Wikipedia-iOS. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 1 says to validate on the Charts/Realm/Wikipedia corpus before moving on and not proceed to Phase 2 until Phase 1 passes the §5a bar on all three repos.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: proposed
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/41e5c818-e207-47e7-abe0-33efa342355c
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/5d9c4afc-c9e8-473a-b47b-141df78b8980
  hasTitle: Phase one bridge gate
  hasTimestamp: 2026-05-26T07:14:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Constraint/be3ea60d-de0c-47f5-a251-7dd2e9d79ef2

• Lesson — "Declared return types define chain fit"
  hasDescription: The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/067da6b3-818a-487a-a67e-930d084dd366
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/e985a51c-4bba-432f-b9d0-d11231c6f439

  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/a5a8137e-bf71-4c6e-83e6-fb8ea23eac6f
  hasTitle: Declared return types define chain fit
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-11T13:06:37Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/fe9054a7-3ce6-4592-ad4c-7e6931dc4805

• Constraint — "Wrong edge drops silently"
  hasDescription: When CodeGraph cannot prove a candidate dependency belongs to the correct receiver, language family, source set, or file scope, it should emit no edge instead of a misleading one. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 C++ wrong guess produces no edge, type references stay within language families, and quoted includes/source sets prefer the correct local target.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/3f6d115d-55cd-4158-8159-ad209a5af878
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/30ebe539-603a-4185-926d-865f5bf1acee
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/5f5cf834-a582-44c1-a4ba-e927b4e63673
  constrains: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/dd12d3d4-e434-4b79-978b-0bb4fefd7dd6
  hasTitle: Wrong edge drops silently
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-22T23:16:11Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Constraint/cb01dfb6-ab66-4204-8781-defbb371b0b1

• Lesson — "Constant read node check"
  hasDescription: A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/1e2b8d0a-6176-4d85-bfee-50353e857d72
  hasTitle: Constant read node check
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/c5b50359-b0bb-4ae4-b5bc-e80e776380c7

• Lesson — "Sample variable targets before trusting"
  hasDescription: Before trusting a new language's `variable` targets for value refs, sample them to confirm they represent module/global shared state rather than parameters or instance fields. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 states this as the Pascal trap after `Dest` and `aItem` were read everywhere because parameter and field variables passed the target gate.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/c359ccd5-e588-43be-9f6e-459340535380
  hasTitle: Sample variable targets before trusting
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/c3eb70fb-7fd6-4f85-92ef-c018e8857594

• Lesson — "Parent-kind sample check"
  hasDescription: Before enabling value references for the next class-scope language, inspect the parent kind of a sample constant and widen the target gate when that shared parent kind is missing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A explicitly calls this the lesson for the next class-scope language and says missing `struct:`, `enum:`, or `interface:`-style parent kinds make the feature silently emit nothing despite nodes existing.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/b7a88544-2269-4bc1-bbe3-242560a809ba
  hasTitle: Parent-kind sample check
  hasTimestamp: 2026-06-16T17:16:00Z
  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/cb181180-4026-4623-be1a-90ef85ce58f0

• Lesson — "Trace wrongness masquerades as adoption floor"
  hasDescription: A small repo read-heavy result can be a fixable trace endpoint bug rather than an adoption floor; compare what the agent read with the tool output immediately before it. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says Alamofire was misread as the small-repo floor until transcripts showed the tool returned wrong stub endpoints, and the methodology lesson says transcript reasoning, not the median, tells which case it is.
  hasAuthor: codegraph docs <bootstrap>
  hasLifecycleStatus: accepted
  learnedFrom: https://moosedev.dev/kg/ArchitecturalDecision/88760684-773f-476a-8fc3-724c8b8eb03d

  https://moosedev.dev/kg/Lesson/4299ba8f-7d57-4764-91e9-f55a6080836e

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Go gRPC implementation bridging"
  hasDescription: Go gRPC interface stubs connect to their hand-written implementations so callers, callees, impact, and trace land on the real method rather than the empty generated stub. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

• ArchitecturalDecision — "Qualified resolution fixes"
  hasDescription: CodeGraph resolution uses concrete language qualification signals for C/C++ includes, Java/Kotlin imports, TypeScript object-shaped aliases, C# type references, Go `go.mod` package calls, and C++ typed member pointers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

• Constraint — "Function-ref validation invariants"
  hasDescription: Function-ref capture must prove node counts identical, `calls` edges unchanged, `references` strictly additive, sampled `fnRef` edges precise, and unresolved ref batches drained. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Validation says the 2026-06-11 A/B used fresh public OSS clones, identical nodes, untouched calls, additive references, source-line spot checks, and fully drained `unresolved_refs`.

• Constraint — "Value-ref PR workflow"
  hasDescription: Value-reference validation and precision work must follow the documented PR hygiene: branch from main, keep pure validation docs/test changes separate from focused precision code fixes when practical, put user-facing changelog entries under Unreleased, include the specified generated-by trailers, and leave merge decisions to the maintainer. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §6 lists the branch, PR split, commit trailer, PR body trailer, maintainer-merge rule, admin squash note, and changelog placement.

• ArchitecturalDecision — "JVM variable method-ref silence"
  hasDescription: Java and Kotlin method references through variables such as `subscriber::onNext` or `m::run0` deliberately emit no edge because the receiver type is statically unknown and prior bare capture produced wrong same-file matches. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says the qualified rework drops variable receiver method refs after RxJava baseline bare capture misresolved them.
